newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Easdaq trading seen starting mid-November.
newsitem.headline: Easdaq trading seen starting mid-November.

text.p: Trading in Europe's new growth stocks market Easdaq is not expected to start until mid-November because of procedural delays slowing listings, the exchange said on Friday.
"... we are now aiming for the middle of November because that's when the first initial public offerings (IPO) are due," Easdaq spokesman Chris Pickles told Reuters.
It was also possible that a couple of the about 80 European companies listed on Nasdaq and now seeking a dual listing on Easdaq would not be able to find market makers for their stock.
Stocks listed on Easdaq must be supported by at least two market makers.
Easdaq board member Marcel Stappers said earlier this month firms listed on Nasdaq were having trouble finding Easdaq market makers because they were less known in Europe.
Pickles said 12 companies were on the list of companies seeking IPOs in the near term.
Nor had the Belgian finance ministry's approval of Easdaq's listing rules yet been published in the state's official journal.
"They should be published next week," he said.
Easdaq, modelled on the U.S. Nasdaq market, beame technically operational on September 30. The exchange is headquartered in Brussels and is supervised by Belgian authorities.
